provider: LUMI-O (CSC / EuroHPC LUMI) — 150 TB allocated per LUMI project by default

free_tier.stated: 'LUMI-O offers a total of 30 PB storage space ... By default 150 TB of storage space is allocated per LUMI project, but projects can request for more LUMI-O storage space by contacting the LUMI helpdesk.' This is the single largest default per-project object-storage quota found in the entire survey.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: No retention clause documented in available terms.

egress.terms: Unmetered; public buckets and presigned URLs are served over HTTPS. 'It is possible to share public data across the internet (for the duration of your project)' and 'to set a temporary access link to otherwise private data'.

tooling: rclone, s3cmd, aws cli, LUMI web interface. Credentials are LUMI-O access tokens generated at auth.lumidata.eu, scoped to a project.
chaining: 150 TB × N LUMI projects. A LUMI project is the unit; Finnish researchers create LUMI projects through MyCSC (the 'LUMI' project category) and LUMI is also reachable through EuroHPC Benchmark/Regular access and through national shares (e.g. SURF's Small Compute applications include 'up to 100,000 TB-hours project space storage' on LUMI). Every LUMI project carries LUMI-O by default: 'All LUMI projects have LUMI-O available by default.'
limits_note: Per-object-cap: 500,000 objects per bucket, same as Allas. No per-object byte cap documented. Retention is the project lifetime, explicitly: 'Data lifetime in LUMI-O is the same as your project lifetime.' request-rate: not published. Note: 'In LUMI-O one project is treated as one account: all project members have the same access/user rights'. So quota is per project, never per person.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

reliability_note: Data dies with the project; no backup is implied and objects cannot be modified in place.

conflicts.class: three readings in the seed: table.md says qualifies, verify/ says fails-identity, and three prose documents agree with verify/
conflicts.resolution: fails-identity: the quota is real and the registration gate is institutional (Haka/Virtu, a home organisation with a CSC contract, or a LUMI/EuroHPC project). No foreign individual without an affiliation can create the project the quota is attached to, so the quota is unreachable and the verdict records the gate, not the byte count. Resolved in this pass; see history/2026-10-22T*Z/storage-csc-allas-verdict.md

extras.agent_focus: National and regional research-data infrastructure that hands out free (or grant-funded) bulk object storage to researchers: EUDAT/B2SHARE, EOSC EU Node, SURF, GÉANT ecosystem, NIRD/Sigma2, CSC Allas + LUMI-O, NAISS, DeiC, EuroHPC, DARIAH/CLARIN/ELIXIR nodes, NCI, ARDC Nectar, Digital Alliance of Canada, ACCESS/OSN, TACC, NCAR, NRP. Central question: which of these are SELF-SERVICE (anyone can get a login and a bucket) versus INSTITUTION-GATED (you need a university appointment, a national research affiliation, or a reviewed proposal). The per-project quotas here are the largest numbers in the whole survey — 10-150 TB — so the gate, not the quota, is the finding.
